re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 93
- **Additions**: +92
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T10:34:31Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +99
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T11:16:18Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 93
- **Additions**: +92
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T10:34:31Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

# gh-1266: [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)

## Description

**Evidence** (nightly run 37260378075, job «flutter_app suite (macOS, non-golden)», step «flutter test (all except integration + goldens)»):
- ❌ test/chat_screen_test.dart: ChatScreen side panels **open_app: the screen installs the launcher and the tool navigates to the app**
- ❌ test/integration/dynamic_message_chip_e2e_test.dart: E2E-mobile: widget stays visible mid-turn, chip opens it ephemerally (#379)
- ❌ test/integration/dynamic_message_live_tile_test.dart: live turn: dynamic_message mounts the interactive tile (#336 AC1)
- ❌ test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart: AgentService.appLauncher the registered tool executes against the service env
- ❌ test/apps/js_theme_test.dart: engine theme plumbing initialTheme reaches JS and updateTheme fires

Five failures in ONE feature area (apps panel / app launcher / dynamic-message tiles) = a regression, not flake. Recent merges touching that code (last 3 days): **b343c68d8 feat(#866) apps panel reflects reality (#1139)** and 6244a390d fix(#1175) one-Fa-one-session FAB (#1173) — prime suspects in that order.

**For the fixer:** reproduce locally (`cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_live_tile_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` on macOS), bisect between the two suspects, fix the behavior or update the tests if the new behavior is intended (then the card must say what changed).

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: macOS suite green in nightly.
- AC2: the breaking commit is named; if a test expectation was intentionally changed by #1139/#1173, the PR that changes the test explains the intended new behavior.
- AC3: if the cluster only fails on CI-macOS (passes locally), say so explicitly and deflake à la #1166 instead of force-adjusting expectations.

Unassigned per owner.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +99
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T11:16:18Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +99
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T11:38:00Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 93
- **Additions**: +92
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T10:34:31Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +99
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T11:16:18Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +99
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T11:38:00Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 93
- **Additions**: +92
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T10:34:31Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +99
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T11:16:18Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +99
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T11:38:00Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 93
- **Additions**: +92
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T10:34:31Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +99
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T11:38:00Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 93
- **Additions**: +92
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T10:34:31Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

## Description

**Evidence** (nightly run 37260378075, job «flutter_app suite (macOS, non-golden)», step «flutter test (all except integration + goldens)»):

- ❌ test/apps/js_theme_test.dart: engine theme plumbing initialTheme reaches JS and updateTheme fires

Recent merges touching that code (last 3 days): **b343c68d8 feat(#866) apps panel reflects reality (#1139)** and 6244a390d fix(#1175) one-Fa-one-session FAB (#1173) — prime suspects in that order.

**For the fixer:** reproduce locally (`cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_live_tile_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` on macOS), bisect between the two suspects, fix the behavior or update the tests if the new behavior is intended (then the card must say what changed).

**Acceptance:**
- AC1: macOS suite green in nightly.
- AC2: the breaking commit is named; if a test expectation was intentionally changed by #1139/#1173, the PR that changes the test explains the intended new behavior.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +99
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T11:16:18Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1278
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1278
- **Title**: gh-1266 [BUG] nightly red: macOS flutter_app suite — 5-test cluster around apps panel / open_app launcher / dynamic_message tiles (suspects #1139, #1173)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1266` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +99
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T10:13:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T11:38:00Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
The 5-test cluster shares one root: the JS-app bootstrap in `JsAppEngine` could not parse on any host where the JS engine actually loads (macOS JavaScriptCore in nightly; Linux QuickJS reproduces it via the issue #184 guard's `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`). Two defects in the gh-1164 fingerprint block of `_faBootstrapJs`: (1) it is a **non-raw** Dart string, so Dart converted the JS `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escapes into real control characters — the regex `/[ \t\r\n]+/g` gained a literal line terminator → `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`; (2) the whitespace-collapse replacement was corrupt — `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` with an unterminated string literal. Bootstrap and widget code are one eval script, so the parse error killed every engine boot: app tiles, dynamic-message tiles, `open_app` navigation, and the launcher smoke gate. Ubuntu CI never saw it because those tests SKIP without the native QuickJS bridge. A second, binding-less-lifecycle bug surfaced once the engine could boot: `JsAppEngine._inWidgetTest` probed `WidgetsBinding.instance` unguarded and threw in plain `test()`s (`open_app_tool_test`).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`:
  - `_faBootstrapJs` is now a raw string (`r'''`) — JS escapes reach the engine verbatim; comment documents the invariant.
  - Repaired both `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ')` lines to `.replace(/[ \t\r\n]+/g, ' ')`.
  - `_inWidgetTest` probes `BindingBase.debugBindingType()` instead of `WidgetsBinding.instance` (null-safe when no binding is initialized).
- `flutter_app/test/apps/open_app_tool_test.dart`: `TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` at `main()` — flutter_js's fetch bootstrap loads its polyfill via the root asset bundle, which needs the services binding once the engine really boots.
- New regression tests: `js_app_engine_test.dart` asserts the bootstrap keeps its JS escape sequences and quoted replacement; `js_app_engine_no_binding_test.dart` (new file, deliberately binding-free) guards dispose without a widget binding.

### Test Coverage
- All 5 nightly failures verified FAIL pre-fix and PASS post-fix with a live QuickJS engine forced via `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` (the exact nightly symptoms: `SyntaxError: unexpected line terminator in regexp`, empty uiTree/exported state).
- Nightly scope, default CI config: `flutter test test/apps test/integration/dynamic_message_*_test.dart test/chat_screen_test.dart` — **451 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full suite (all except integration + goldens): **3404 passed, 53 failed** — the 49 real failures are byte-identical to a base-commit (`fc23b43`) run of the same files (CLI-visual PTY, wasm toolchain, providers-queue IO — pre-existing Linux-environment issues, zero regressions; 4 extra are helper .dart files pulled in as entrypoints by my glob, not test failures).

### Notes
- **AC2**: the ticket's suspects (#1139/#1173) are not the cause — the regression lives in the gh-1164 bootstrap block. The checkout's git history is squashed, so the exact breaking commit cannot be named.
- **AC3**: not a macOS-only flake — the failures are deterministic wherever the JS engine loads; reproducing locally on Linux only requires pointing `LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH` at the flutter_js-bundled bridge.
- Out of scope, observed while forcing the engine: `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` has 2 tests that fail ONLY on the QuickJS path (flutter_js jsonDecodes the `__jsr_log` payload, so the `{iid,id}` wrapper reaches `_handleLog` as a Map; the JSC/macOS path unwraps it). They pass on macOS nightly and skip on Ubuntu CI — pre-existing divergence in the vendored `flutter_js_widget_runtime`, left untouched.
- `[REDACTED:Credential File]` placeholder was created locally (gitignored, mirrors the CI workflow's `touch .env`).
